messages:
lina: Heads up — got a high burn-rate alert for svc/model-serving SLO around 03:20 UTC. Alert name is `slo_burn_high`. The alert link just points to the rule, not the graph. Where's the canonical burn graph and the raw error logs? :eyes:
sam: For graphs: Observability -> SLOs -> model-serving. Direct link: https://observability.redwood.ai/dashboards/slo/model-serving (opens the 30m burn chart). For raw errors, we keep request/error logs in Loki with label `service="model-serving"`. Use the logs app from that dashboard. :+1:
joel: If you want the burn rate prom query quickly, try this PromQL in Grafana:```
sum(rate(slo_error_count{service="model-serving"}[5m])) / sum(rate(slo_total_count{service="model-serving"}[5m]))
```This gives recent error rate; compare to `slo_target` to compute burn.
maya: Also check traces for increased tail latency — could be cascading failures rather than pure 5xxs. Traces link: https://tracing.redwood.ai/trace-search?service=model-serving
eng-sre-bot: alert `slo_burn_high` triggered at 2026-03-17T03:20:14Z; affected env=prod; severity=page. On-call: joel.
joel: I'm on it, looking at the dashboard now. Early note: I see a spike in 5xxs from a single host pool (gpu-pool-7). Can someone paste the `kubectl logs` tail for the failing pod?
lina: grabbing logs now, pasting tail —```
[2026-03-17T03:20:12Z] ERROR request_id=abcd1234 status=503 model=rw-instruct msg="context timeout"
[2026-03-17T03:20:13Z] ERROR request_id=abcd1235 status=502 model=rw-instruct msg="upstream reset"
[2026-03-17T03:20:14Z] ERROR request_id=abcd1236 status=503 model=rw-instruct msg="kv cache miss + timeout"
```Looks like upstream timeouts clustered during that minute.
sam: That matches metrics: network error rate for gpu-pool-7 spiked. Suggest we reduce alert sensitivity for the burn rule to 10m window with 3x burn threshold, and create a follow-up to tune based on host pool noise.
joel: For now I'll silence the pager for this rule for 15 minutes and create an incident ticket if we see recurrence. Creating ticket: https://issues.redwood.ai/INC-2026
maya: FYI we should also add a note in the SLO runbook: mapping of host-pool anomalies -> temporary silencing + host pool draining play. I can draft that.
lina: thanks — I'll attach the pod logs to INC-2026 and mark root-cause candidate as upstream timeouts from gpu-pool-7.
joel: Closing loop: no sustained burn after 03:30 UTC, marking as recovery. Recommend follow-up task to adjust burn alert aggregation and add host-pool filter to reduce noisy alerts. :white_check_mark:
